mainTopic: Why רבי יהושע בן לוי needed two rulings on עירוב, and the rules for deciding הלכה between תנאים, which רב משרשיא challenges
overview: The גמרא gives two more reasons why רבי יהושע בן לוי needed two rulings about עירוב. רב פפא says we might have been lenient only in עירובי חצירות and not in עירובי תחומין. רב אשי says we might have been lenient only in שיורי עירוב and not in תחילת עירוב. Each distinction is proven from a משנה, one of רבי יהודה and one of רבי יוסי. The גמרא then brings general rules for deciding between תנאים. רבי עקיבא, רבי יוסי, and רבי usually win, and there is a ranking of רבי יוסי above רבי יהודה, and רבי יהודה above רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון. The question of רבי מאיר against רבי שמעון stays as תיקו. רב משרשיא says these rules cannot be relied on. The גמרא searches for his source: a first proof is rejected, and a second משנה, about a city that changes ownership, begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפא: we might have thought leniency applies only to עירובי חצירות
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new reason why רבי יהושע בן לוי needed both rulings. The general lenient rule might have been limited to עירובי חצירות, so a specific ruling was needed for עירובי תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: It was necessary. You might have thought that this applies only to עירובי חצירות. But for עירובי תחומין, I would say no, so it was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers another answer to the earlier question of why רבי יהושע בן לוי gave two rulings. He says that without the specific ruling, we might have limited the general leniency to courtyard עירובין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule 'follow the lenient opinion in עירוב' might have been understood to cover only עירובי חצירות, which are fully דרבנן. The case of רבי יוחנן בן נורי deals with תחומין, which are treated more strictly. So a specific ruling was needed to show that we are lenient there too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary (both statements were needed)
It might have entered your mind to say (the mistaken assumption)
These words apply only to…
עירובין that join courtyards so people may carry between them
עירובין that extend how far one may walk on שבת

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said: It was necessary,
because it would have entered your mind to say:
these words apply only to eiruvin of courtyards,
phrases.notes: "These words" means the general rule that we're lenient with עירוב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּעֵירוּבֵי תְחוּמִין — אֵימָא לָא צְרִיכָא.
phrases.english: but regarding eiruvin of Shabbat limits, I would say not. [Therefore] it was necessary.
phrases.notes: Some read צריכא as the closing word: 'therefore both statements were needed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the question raised on the previous amud: why did רבי יהושע בן לוי need two rulings?
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each statement teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general leniency in עירוב applies only to עירובי חצירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The specific ruling shows that leniency applies to עירובי תחומין as well.

steps.title: How do we know עירובי חצירות and עירובי תחומין are treated differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that the הלכה really distinguishes between עירובי חצירות and עירובי תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that we distinguish between עירובי חצירות and עירובי תחומין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check the basis of רב פפא's answer. This line sets up the next step, where a source will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's answer only works if there is a real reason to treat the two kinds of עירוב differently. The גמרא wants a source showing that such a distinction exists elsewhere in the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say? (asking for a source)
We distinguish / it differs for us

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that we distinguish between eiruvin of courtyards
and eiruvin of Shabbat limits?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the distinction that רב פפא relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that עירובי חצירות and עירובי תחומין follow different rules.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's משנה: an עירוב חצירות can be made without the person knowing
steps.stepSummary: A משנה quotes רבי יהודה. A person's knowledge is required only for עירובי תחומין. עירובי חצירות may be made without his knowledge, because זכין לאדם שלא בפניו.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה said: When was this said? For עירובי תחומין. But for עירובי חצירות, we may make an עירוב for someone whether he knows or not. This is because you may do something good for a person when he is not there, but you may do something bad for him only in his presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the distinction from a משנה. There, רבי יהודה treats the two types of עירוב differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירובי חצירות only helps a person, so others may set it up for him without asking. An עירובי תחומין lets him walk farther in one direction but takes away the other direction, so it also harms him. That is why it needs his consent. This shows the הלכה does treat the two kinds differently.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case were these words said? (limiting a rule)
With his knowledge
One may act for a person's benefit without his presence
Act to someone's disadvantage

steps.confusionAlert: The distinction here is about whether the person must know about the עירוב. It is not about leniency in a doubt. The גמרא brings it only to show that the two kinds of עירוב are not treated the same.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda said:
In what case were these words said?
phrases.notes: This is asking about the rule that you can make an עירוב for someone only if he knows about it.

phrases.english: Regarding eiruvin of Shabbat limits;
but regarding eiruvin of courtyards,

phrases.aramaic: מְעָרְבִין בֵּין לְדַעַת וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת,
phrases.english: one may make an eiruv whether with his knowledge or without his knowledge,
because one may act in a person's favor not in his presence,
but one may not act to a person's disadvantage except in his presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by bringing a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה distinguishes between עירובי חצירות and עירובי תחומין, which supports רב פפא's answer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה with רבי יהודה's statement about making an עירוב with or without the person's knowledge.

steps.title: רב אשי: we might have thought leniency applies only to an existing עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives another reason both rulings were needed. The general leniency might have been limited to שיורי עירוב, an עירוב that already exists, and not applied to תחילת עירוב, a new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It was necessary. You might have thought that this applies only to the remains of an עירוב. But for the start of an עירוב, I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers yet another answer to why רבי יהושע בן לוי made two rulings. This time the distinction is between an existing עירוב and a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being lenient about an עירוב that was already properly set up is easier to accept. Being lenient when a new עירוב is first being made is harder. The ruling following רבי יוחנן בן נורי is about whether a new עירוב takes effect. So it was needed to teach leniency even at the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Remnants of an עירוב: an already established עירוב that later shrank or may have become invalid
The start of an עירוב: setting it up for the first time
I would say no

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It was necessary,
because it would have entered your mind to say,
these words apply only to the remnants of an eiruv,
but regarding the start of an eiruv, I would say not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer, parallel to רב פפא's, to the same question of why two rulings were needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each statement teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leniency applies only to an existing עירוב (שיורי עירוב).
steps.terutzMaskana: The specific ruling teaches leniency even for תחילת עירוב.

steps.title: How do we know an existing עירוב and a new עירוב are treated differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that שיורי עירוב and תחילת עירוב are treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that we distinguish between the remains of an עירוב and the start of an עירוב?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as with רב פפא, the גמרא asks for proof of the distinction that רב אשי relied on. This sets up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's answer depends on there being a real difference between a new עירוב and an existing one. The גמרא wants evidence of that difference.

phrases.english: And from where do you say that we distinguish
between the remnants of an eiruv and the start of an eiruv?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רב אשי's distinction, the same way step 2 did for רב פפא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that שיורי עירוב and תחילת עירוב have different rules.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's משנה: an existing עירוב needs only a tiny amount
steps.stepSummary: A משנה quotes רבי יוסי. The fixed food amount is required only at the start of an עירוב. For the remains of an עירוב, any amount at all is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יוסי said: When was this said? For the start of an עירוב. But for the remains of an עירוב, even the smallest amount is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רב אשי's distinction from a משנה. In it, רבי יוסי is more lenient about an existing עירוב than a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new עירוב needs the full required amount of food. Once it exists, even a tiny leftover keeps it valid. This shows that the הלכה treats an existing עירוב more leniently than a new one, which supports רב אשי.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even the smallest

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי's two rulings are both needed. Each of the answers here (רב פפא and רב אשי) points to a real distinction in עירוב law, and each is proven from a משנה. For רב פפא, the distinction is עירובי חצירות versus עירובי תחומין, from רבי יהודה. For רב אשי, it is שיורי עירוב versus תחילת עירוב, from רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yosei said:
In what case were these words said?
phrases.notes: Referring to the required minimum amount of food for an עירוב

phrases.english: Regarding the start of an eiruv;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּשִׁיּוּרֵי עֵירוּב — אֲפִילּוּ כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.english: but regarding the remnants of an eiruv, even any amount at all [suffices].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by bringing a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה distinguishes between שיורי עירוב and תחילת עירוב, which supports רב אשי's answer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה with רבי יוסי's statement that the fixed amount is needed only at the start of an עירוב.

steps.title: Why we still make a courtyard עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The last line of the quoted source: courtyards still make their own עירוב so that children don't forget the laws of עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only required making an עירוב for courtyards so that the law of עירוב would not be forgotten by the children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the source it quoted in the last step. This line is a side detail at the end of that source, not a new argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the whole alley is already joined with one food item (שיתוף מבואות), each courtyard still makes its own עירוב. Strictly speaking it may not be needed. The reason is educational: children who see no עירוב being made might forget that such a law exists.

keyTerms.meaning: to make an עירוב joining courtyards
the law/concept of עירוב
children

steps.whatToRemember: This closes the discussion of רבי יוסי's source: a new עירוב needs a fixed amount, leftovers need any amount, and courtyard עירובין are kept so children remember the law.

phrases.english: And they did not say to make an eiruv for courtyards,
except in order not to cause to be forgotten
phrases.notes: The rule exists for an educational reason.

phrases.english: the law of eiruv from the children.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לְעָרֵב חֲצֵירוֹת, אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא לְשַׁכֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation and close of the source quoted in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: Completes the text of the source being cited.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (introduced by דִּתְנַן in step 6) containing רבי יוסי's statement about תחילת עירוב and שיורי עירוב. This line is that משנה's closing clause.

steps.title: Rules for deciding: רבי עקיבא, רבי יוסי, and רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב and רבי זריקא give three rules: the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא against one colleague, רבי יוסי even against several colleagues, and רבי against one colleague.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב and רבי זריקא said: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא against his colleague, רבי יוסי against his colleagues, and רבי against his colleague.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. Earlier it discussed rules for deciding the הלכה, so now it brings more such rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the wording. רבי עקיבא and רבי win against "his colleague" (חבירו, one person). רבי יוסי wins against "his colleagues" (חבריו, plural). This means רבי יוסי's opinion is accepted even against several other חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: the law follows (the opinion of)
against his (single) colleague
against his colleagues (plural)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't skip the difference between חבירו (one) and חבריו (many). That small letter is what gives רבי יוסי a stronger rule than the others.
steps.whyThisMatters: These are practical rules that פוסקים use to decide arguments between תנאים all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov and Rabbi Zerika said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Akiva against his colleague,
and follows Rabbi Yosei against his colleagues,
phrases.notes: "Colleagues" is plural, so this holds even when several Sages disagree with him.

phrases.english: and follows Rebbi against his colleague.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב וְרַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמְרוּ: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about rules of deciding, linked to the earlier discussion of rules of deciding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא against a single colleague, רבי יוסי even against multiple colleagues, and רבי against a single colleague.

steps.title: How binding are these rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what level of authority these deciding rules have.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what kind of הלכה (how binding) were these rules said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about the rules it just heard. It is setting up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not whether the rules are true. It asks how strong they are. Are they taught publicly as firm law, or are they just a guideline?

keyTerms.meaning: for what practical law? / to what degree is this binding?

phrases.english: With regard to what halakha (to what degree are they binding)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the strength of the rules given in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The level of authority of the deciding rules of רבי יעקב and רבי זריקא.

steps.title: Three levels: הלכה, מטין, נראין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי says the rules are full הלכה. רבי חייא בר אבא says מטין, we lean toward them. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says נראין, they only seem right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: It is הלכה. רבי חייא בר אבא said: We lean toward it. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: It appears so.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים answer the question, each giving a different level of strength to the rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels, from strongest to weakest. הלכה: taught publicly as firm law. מטין: not announced publicly, but if someone asks, we steer him this way. נראין: it seems correct, so if someone already acted this way we don't make him undo it, but we don't instruct it.

keyTerms.meaning: we lean (toward this ruling): not taught publicly, but told to one who asks
it appears (correct): accepted after the fact, but not instructed

steps.whatToRemember: There are three strengths of a deciding rule: הלכה (public law), מטין (told to one who asks), and נראין (accepted only after the fact).

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said: It is halakha (binding law).

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: מַטִּין.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said: We incline (toward it).

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: נִרְאִין.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: It appears (correct).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three views on the strength of the rules: הלכה (רבי אסי), מטין (רבי חייא בר אבא), נראין (רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ranking: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that רבי יהודה beats רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי beats רבי יהודה. So clearly רבי יוסי beats רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a similar style, רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. Between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. And needless to say, between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. After all, if רבי מאיר loses against רבי יהודה, is there any question that he loses against רבי יוסי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another set of deciding rules, from רבי יוחנן, in the same style as the previous rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Think of it as a ladder: רבי מאיר is below רבי יהודה, and רבי יהודה is below רבי יוסי. So רבי יוסי must also be above רבי מאיר. That third rule is "needless to say" because it follows by simple קל וחומר: if רבי מאיר loses to the weaker one, he surely loses to the stronger one.

keyTerms.meaning: in the same way (the same three views, הלכה, מטין and נראין, apply to this rule too)
and needless to say
now if (in the weaker case) ..., is it even a question (in the stronger case)?
is not (accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: The ranking is רבי יוסי above רבי יהודה, and רבי יהודה above רבי מאיר. So in a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "needless to say" is not a new rule from a new source. It is a logical result of the first two rules, which the last line spells out.
steps.whyThisMatters: These ranking rules are some of the most commonly used tools for deciding between these three תנאים, who argue very often in the משנה.

phrases.english: In a similar formulation,
phrases.notes: This ties back to the rules for deciding the law that came just before.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda: the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei: the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei.
And needless to say,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei: the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei.
Now, if against Rabbi Yehuda his view (Rabbi Meir's) is not accepted,
against Rabbi Yosei is it even a question?!

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another set of deciding rules, parallel to step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי מאיר, רבי יוסי over רבי יהודה, and certainly רבי יוסי over רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רב אסי adds a rule: רבי יוסי beats רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says he can work out another rule: when רבי יוסי argues with רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: I can also learn a rule from this. When רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון argue, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי adds a new rule to the list: רבי יוסי beats רבי שמעון. His reason comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not quote this rule from a teacher. He works it out himself ("אף אני לומד") from rules that were already stated.

keyTerms.meaning: I too can learn it (work it out by reasoning)

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
I too can learn (a rule):
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon —
the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: אַף אֲנִי לוֹמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי יוחנן's chain of rules from step 11 to a new pair of תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a dispute between רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The proof: if רבי יהודה beats רבי שמעון, surely רבי יוסי does
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן ruled that רבי יהודה beats רבי שמעון. רבי יוסי beats רבי יהודה, so he certainly beats רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: when רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. Now, if רבי שמעון loses even to רבי יהודה, do we even need to say that he loses to רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי proves his rule using a ruling from רבי יוחנן and simple ranking logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Think of it as a ladder: רבי יוסי is above רבי יהודה, and רבי יהודה is above רבי שמעון. If רבי שמעון cannot beat רבי יהודה, he cannot beat רבי יוסי, who is ranked even higher.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (opens a 'how much more so' argument)
In the place of, when facing (an opposing opinion)
It does not stand, it is not accepted
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon —
the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
Now, if against Rabbi Yehuda (Rabbi Shimon's view) does not stand,
against Rabbi Yosei, is it even a question?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב אסי's rule in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that רבי יוסי beats רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that רבי יהודה beats רבי שמעון, combined with the earlier rule that רבי יוסי beats רבי יהודה

steps.title: What about רבי מאיר against רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view wins when רבי מאיר argues with רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: when רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון argue, what is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an open question about a pair of תנאים that the rules do not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ladder trick does not work here. Both רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון lose to רבי יהודה, so we have no way to tell which of the two is ranked higher.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them (opens a genuine question; whether it gets answered depends on what follows)
What (is the law)?

phrases.english: They raised a question:
Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon, what (is the law)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two pairs were settled by the ladder logic, the גמרא asks about a pair that logic cannot settle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose view is the הלכה when רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון argue?

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question stands as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It remains unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer, and the question about רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו is not a ruling for either side. It only means that no source was found to settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the two views are equal or that both are correct. It means only that the question was never answered.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 14 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no established rule for רבי מאיר against רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: these deciding rules do not hold
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says the rules for deciding הלכה between תנאים are not to be relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: these rules do not hold.
steps.whatsHappening: A new and opposing view: רב משרשיא rejects the whole set of deciding rules listed above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא only argued about how strong the rules are (full הלכה, מטין, or נראין). רב משרשיא goes much further and says we cannot rely on them at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not (valid, reliable)
Rules, general principles

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
These rules do not hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: לֵיתַנְהוּ לְהָנֵי כְּלָלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the whole system of rules built in steps 8–13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rules for deciding הלכה between specific תנאים are not to be relied on.
steps.whyThisMatters: If רב משרשיא is right, the rules from steps 8–13 cannot be used to decide הלכה.

steps.title: Where did רב משרשיא learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רב משרשיא based his claim on.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רב משרשיא know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רב משרשיא's claim. This sets up the next step, where it tests a possible source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rejecting accepted rules is a big claim. The גמרא wants to see which text shows that these rules break down.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he (know it)?

phrases.english: From where does Rav Mesharshiya get this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the deciding rules are not reliable.

steps.title: A suggested source: רבי שמעון's three courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רב משרשיא may have learned it from a משנה where רבי שמעון compares a case to three courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he learned it from the משנה where רבי שמעון says: What is this like? Like three courtyards that open into each other and also open into the public domain. If the two outer courtyards made an עירוב with the middle one, the middle one may carry with them and they may carry with it. But the two outer courtyards may not carry with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts testing a possible source for רב משרשיא by quoting רבי שמעון's courtyard example. The argument continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each outer courtyard is joined to the middle one, but the two outer courtyards never joined each other, so carrying between them is not allowed. The word אילימא ("if you say") hints that this suggestion may be tested and possibly rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that may be rejected)
To what is this comparable?
Courtyards
Public domain
The outer ones
The middle one

steps.confusionAlert: Each outer courtyard is joined to the middle, but that does not join the two outer courtyards to each other. Being linked to the same middle courtyard does not link them together.

phrases.english: If you say (he learned it) from what we learned in the Mishnah:
Rabbi Shimon says:
To what is this comparable?
To three courtyards that open into one another
and also open into the public domain.
If the two outer ones made an eiruv with the middle one —
it (the middle) is permitted (to carry) with them
and they are permitted (to carry) with it,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁתַּיִם הַחִיצוֹנוֹת אֲסוּרוֹת זוֹ עִם זוֹ.
phrases.english: but the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggested source: the משנה of רבי שמעון's three courtyards. The analysis of this source continues next.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי שמעון against רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in the three-courtyards case, and the גמרא notes that the one who disagrees with him is רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: the הלכה is like רבי שמעון. And who disagrees with him? רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues building the proof for רב משרשיא from the three-courtyards משנה. It brings רב's ruling there and points out who his opponent is, which sets up the contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 brought the משנה where רבי שמעון compares the case to three courtyards. Now we learn that רב rules like רבי שמעון there. The key detail is that the other side is רבי יהודה, and this matters because of the known rule about רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
Disagrees with him

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Shimon.
And who disagrees with him?
Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof begun in step 18 by bringing רב's ruling on that משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב משרשיא's claim that the rules for deciding between תנאים are unreliable
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון against רבי יהודה in the three-courtyards case

steps.title: The ruling contradicts the general rule, so the rules must be unreliable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב's ruling clashes with the rule that הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון, and concludes that the rules cannot be relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say that between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון the הלכה is like רבי יהודה? So isn't it clear from here that these rules don't hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. רב's ruling goes against the general rule, so it seems the general rules are not reliable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule says that in a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, we follow רבי יהודה. Yet רב follows רבי שמעון against רבי יהודה. If רב can rule against the rule, the rule must not be binding, which is exactly what רב משרשיא claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? (pointing out a contradiction)
So isn't it clear to learn from this?
They do not exist, meaning these rules don't hold

phrases.english: But didn't you say:
In a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon,
the halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda.
Rather, isn't it clear to conclude from this:
that these rules do not hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב's ruling from step 19 to complete the proof for רב משרשיא.
steps.raayaObject: רב משרשיא's claim that the rules are unreliable
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contradiction between רב's ruling and the rule that הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון

steps.title: The proof is rejected because the rules only apply where nothing explicit was said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the general rules may apply only where there is no explicit ruling, and here רב gave one.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Maybe where an explicit ruling was stated, it was stated, and where it was not stated, it was not stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. רב's ruling does not show that the rules are worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rules are default guides for cases where no specific ruling exists. When an אמורא like רב gives an explicit ruling for a specific case, that ruling overrides the default. So the rules still hold everywhere else, and רב משרשיא's source must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (rejecting a proof)
Perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the general rules. It only limits them to cases with no explicit ruling.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps where an explicit ruling was stated, it was stated,
and where it was not stated, it was not stated (and the rules apply).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 19 and 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole first proof for רב משרשיא's source
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An explicit ruling for a specific case does not cancel general default rules. The rules only apply where nothing explicit was said.

steps.title: A second source: the משנה about a city that changes ownership
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a different source for רב משרשיא: a משנה about making an ערוב for a city that changes from private to public ownership, or from public to private, starting with רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is from what we learned in a משנה: a city that belonged to one person and became a city of many people may have one ערוב for all of it. A city of many people that became owned by one person may not have one ערוב for all of it, unless he leaves a part outside the ערוב the size of the town חדשה in יהודה, which has fifty residents. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a second attempt to find רב משרשיא's source. It quotes a משנה and gives רבי יהודה's view. The last words open רבי שמעון's view, which continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A city that was once privately owned never had a public domain, so one ערוב can cover all of it. A city that was once public had public areas, so a section must be left out of the ערוב so people remember the area's original public status. רבי יהודה sets the size of that section at a town like חדשה with fifty residents. The גמרא will use the dispute with רבי שמעון to try to prove that the rules are unreliable.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from what we learned in a משנה (a new attempt)
A city owned by one person
We make an ערוב (joining areas to allow carrying on שבת)
Outside of it, meaning a section left out of the ערוב
Residents

phrases.english: Rather, it is from what we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: עִיר שֶׁל יָחִיד וְנַעֲשֵׂית שֶׁל רַבִּים —
phrases.english: A city that belonged to one person and became a city of many people,
one may make an eruv for all of it.
A city of many people that became owned by one person,
one may not make an eruv for all of it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עוֹשֶׂה חוּצָה לָהּ,
phrases.english: unless he leaves out an area outside the eruv,
like the size of the town Chadasha in Judea,
which has fifty residents;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Shimon says:
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון's words continue in the next section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first source was rejected in step 21, this offers a new source for רב משרשיא's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רב משרשיא's claim (from step 17)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה about a city that changes ownership, in which רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree
